title: Mesopotamian cuneiform commentaries (mukallimtu/ṣâtu) – 'Babylonian scholia'; unit: commentaries on literary works (Enūma eliš VII, Ludlul, Theodicy, Lugale) / Месопотамские клинописные комментарии
author: Anonymous Assyrian and Babylonian scholars (ummânū)
size: 882 catalogue entries (CCP); pilot c. 10–15 tablets, est. under 1,000 lines
edition: CCP online editions (Frahm, Jiménez et al.) under CC BY-SA 4.0 (ccp.yale.edu/citation-guidelines); Frahm, Babylonian and Assyrian Text Commentaries (2011). Photos copyright of the museums.
ru_evidence: No Russian translation found. CyberLeninka 'клинописные комментарии' returns only studies; no ru.wikipedia article on the genre.
en_evidence: CCP gives annotated English translations for part of the 882 catalogue entries (ccp.yale.edu/catalogue); many remain unedited.
other_translations: Scattered German/French in articles; no full corpus translation found.
value: Earliest systematic commentary tradition, parallel to Greek scholia and Alexandrian philology. Key for hermeneutics, the milieu of Berossus and the history of science. A programmatic match for the 'Neoscholia' name.
ai_feasibility: medium: transliterations exist, but etymological wordplay, polyvalent signs and Sumerian equations need expert control. An ideal showcase for visible multi-model review.
pilot_unit: CCP literary section: commentaries on Enūma eliš VII (names of Marduk), Ludlul, Theodicy; c. 10–15 tablets
